name: Cell Sleep Energy Saver
use_case: O-RAN UC21 cell switch on/off energy saving
description: Cell Sleep Energy Saver rApp (O-RAN UC21 cell switch on/off energy saving). Ranks lightly loaded cells or carriers for sleep, switches them off and restores them when load returns (writes cell_power). Use when the goal is to cut RAN energy consumption by switching cells or carriers off in low-traffic periods, or to bring sleeping cells back. Do not use when capacity has to be added, coverage reshaped or individual users prioritised, or the cell must stay on and only MIMO layers / RF channels are to be muted (MIMO sleep); declared conflict with capacity-boost functions. Emulated rApp served by rapps/runtime.py: decisions are simple estimators over live KPM; apply tools write an A1-style policy document that is not enforced on the RAN.

tools.label: Recommend Sleep Cells
tools.description: Rank cells for deep sleep from PRB utilisation.

tools.label: Apply Cell Sleep
tools.description: Switch the selected cells off via RC and confirm.

tools.label: Wake Cells
tools.description: Restore switched-off cells.

name: Traffic Steering
description: Traffic Steering rApp (O-RAN UC1 traffic steering). Computes load-balancing handover targets and pushes a per-UE steering policy (writes UE-level rc_control). Use when traffic has to be moved between cells or carriers, e.g. offloading a congested cell onto its neighbours. Do not use when the fix is a transport queue policy or a slice reservation, or the load balance should be shifted for all users by changing cell-level handover offsets (mobility load balancing); it must not run after a cell_power writer (declared conflict). Emulated rApp served by rapps/runtime.py: decisions are simple estimators over live KPM; apply tools write an A1-style policy document that is not enforced on the RAN.

name: Mobility Robustness Optimizer
description: Mobility Robustness Optimizer rApp (Mobility robustness optimisation (MRO)). Detects handover oscillation and tunes A3 offset / time-to-trigger per cell pair (writes cell-level rc_control). Use when handover failures or too-early, too-late or oscillating handovers have to be reduced by changing handover parameters. Do not use when the problem is load imbalance between cells (traffic steering or mobility load balancing) or transport delay; declared conflict with cell-offset load balancing, which tunes the same handover triggers. Emulated rApp served by rapps/runtime.py: decisions are simple estimators over live KPM; apply tools write an A1-style policy document that is not enforced on the RAN.

Use when energy has to be saved on massive-MIMO cells that cannot be switched off because they still carry traffic, by reducing active antennas or MIMO layers. Do not use when whole cells or carriers can be switched off at low load (cell sleep energy saving) or capacity must be boosted; declared conflict with capacity-boost and beam-pattern changes. Emulated rApp served by rapps/runtime.py: decisions are simple estimators over live KPM; apply tools write an A1-style policy document that is not enforced on the RAN.

name: RAN Fault Predictor
use_case: RAN fault prediction / predictive maintenance (3GPP TS 28.104 MDA)
description: RAN Fault Predictor rApp (RAN fault prediction / predictive maintenance (3GPP TS 28.104 MDA)). Predicts imminent RAN hardware or cell faults from PM, power and alarm trends and recommends preventive maintenance. Read-only. Use when faults have to be anticipated before they happen, e.g. which radios or sites are likely to fail and should get preventive maintenance. Do not use when a fault already happened and has to be explained (root cause analysis) or compensated; it never changes RAN state. Emulated rApp served by rapps/runtime.py: decisions are simple estimators over live KPM; apply tools write an A1-style policy document that is not enforced on the RAN.

tools.label: Predict Faults

name: Slice Admission Controller
use_case: Tenant / slice-aware admission control (O-RAN slicing, 3GPP TS 23.501 NSAC)
description: Slice Admission Controller rApp (Tenant / slice-aware admission control (O-RAN slicing, 3GPP TS 23.501 NSAC)). Admits or rejects new sessions per slice or tenant against slice quotas and current load, protecting the guaranteed slices (writes slice_admission). Use when new users or sessions of a slice or tenant have to be admitted, capped or rejected (admission control, quota per tenant). Do not use when the PRB reservation of a slice has to be changed (slice SLA assurance / SLICE xApp), or one user needs priority (QoS priority control). Emulated rApp served by rapps/runtime.py: decisions are simple estimators over live KPM; apply tools write an A1-style policy document that is not enforced on the RAN.

tools.label: Evaluate Admission
tools.description: Compute per-slice admission headroom from load and quotas.

tools.label: Apply Admission Policy
tools.description: Push per-slice admission limits and confirm.

name: Signalling Storm Protector
description: Signalling Storm Protector rApp (Signalling storm protection (O-RAN UC15)). Detects signalling storms (abnormal bursts of RRC connection attempts from many UEs or devices) and throttles or rejects the offending connection requests (writes rrc_admission). Use when a flood of connection or registration attempts, e.g. from misbehaving IoT devices, overloads the control plane and has to be detected and throttled. Do not use when access failures are caused by RACH configuration (RACH optimisation) or admission per slice quota is wanted (slice admission control). Emulated rApp served by rapps/runtime.py: decisions are simple estimators over live KPM; apply tools write an A1-style policy document that is not enforced on the RAN.

tools.label: Detect Signalling Storm
tools.description: Flag cells with abnormal connection-attempt bursts.

tools.label: Apply Throttling Policy
tools.description: Throttle or reject the offending connection requests.

name: Uplink Interference Optimizer
use_case: Uplink interference detection and power-control optimisation (3GPP TS 38.300 RIM context)
description: Uplink Interference Optimizer rApp (Uplink interference detection and power-control optimisation (3GPP TS 38.300 RIM context)). Detects and classifies uplink interference (external, traffic-induced, infrastructure) and retunes uplink power control (P0 nominal PUSCH, alpha) per cell (writes ul_power_control). Use when uplink SINR or uplink throughput is degraded by interference or a raised noise floor and uplink power control has to be retuned. Do not use when the interference is in the downlink (interference mitigation by power caps) or comes from a PCI clash (PCI optimisation). Emulated rApp served by rapps/runtime.py: decisions are simple estimators over live KPM; apply tools write an A1-style policy document that is not enforced on the RAN.

tools.label: Detect Ul Interference
tools.description: Classify uplink-interfered cells by interference type.

tools.label: Apply Ul Power Control
tools.description: Apply P0/alpha changes via O1 and confirm.

name: EN-DC Traffic Optimizer
description: EN-DC Traffic Optimizer rApp (5G NSA (EN-DC) traffic optimisation). Steers EN-DC (NSA) devices between LTE anchors and NR legs by retuning dual-connectivity distribution profiles from NR and LTE load (writes dc_profile). Use when traffic of 5G NSA / EN-DC devices has to be rebalanced between the LTE anchor and the NR secondary cell, e.g. NR legs overloaded or under-used. Do not use when the users are 5G standalone or the steering is between cells of the same RAT (traffic steering, mobility load balancing). Emulated rApp served by rapps/runtime.py: decisions are simple estimators over live KPM; apply tools write an A1-style policy document that is not enforced on the RAN.

name: Configuration Consistency Auditor
description: Configuration Consistency Auditor rApp (Configuration consistency audit). Audits configuration (CM) consistency across cells and sites against a golden baseline and lists deviating parameters. Read-only. Use when parameter settings have to be checked for inconsistencies or drift from the baseline, e.g. after a rollout or before a change. Do not use when configuration has to be changed or rolled out (RAN lifecycle orchestration) or KPI deviations are the question (KPI anomaly detection); it never changes RAN state. Emulated rApp served by rapps/runtime.py: decisions are simple estimators over live KPM; apply tools write an A1-style policy document that is not enforced on the RAN.

name: Crossed Feeder Detector
description: Crossed Feeder Detector rApp (Crossed feeder detection). Detects crossed feeders / swapped sectors from UE measurement reports, handover patterns and site topology. Read-only. Use when installation errors such as crossed feeders or swapped sector cabling are suspected, e.g. after a site build or antenna swap, or handovers go to the wrong sector. Do not use when handover parameters or neighbour lists are the problem (mobility robustness, neighbour relation management); it never changes RAN state. Emulated rApp served by rapps/runtime.py: decisions are simple estimators over live KPM; apply tools write an A1-style policy document that is not enforced on the RAN.

tools.label: Detect Crossed Feeders
tools.description: Rank sectors by crossed-feeder likelihood.

name: Special Event Handler
description: Special Event Handler rApp (Special event handling). Applies a temporary capacity profile (parameter set) to the cells around a planned event and reverts it afterwards (writes event_profile). Use when a planned mass event (concert, match, fair) needs a temporary capacity configuration for a fixed time window that is reverted afterwards. Do not use when the change is permanent (RAN lifecycle orchestration) or unplanned congestion has to be relieved now (traffic steering); declared conflict with energy saving, which would switch the boosted cells off. Emulated rApp served by rapps/runtime.py: decisions are simple estimators over live KPM; apply tools write an A1-style policy document that is not enforced on the RAN.
